transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The program would involve 24 students meeting twice weekly during the spring semester, using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with one STEM teacher supervising. I'd like to hear from each of you on the implementation aspects relevant to your roles so I can make an informed decision. Could we start with you?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share the results of my room-safety review, which I completed this week. The review found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, which would not meet these safety requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share the results of my health-record review of the participating students. I found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share a concern regarding the technology workflow. I confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage. The approved workflow is an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan. However, the draft program still instructs students to use cloud-based computer-aided design files, and I have not yet replaced that cloud-storage instruction in the draft.
transcript.speaker: A4

Add the health-record review to the program file and ensure the materials list is approved by the nurse before each session, using only nickel-free components.
Replace the cloud-storage instruction in the draft program with the approved offline design workstation and encrypted USB transfer workflow.
Determine how to provide a second supervising adult for soldering sessions given the program meets twice weekly with one STEM teacher currently assigned.
